processing: A local tea plant rather than a finished tea. Processing depends on the tea made from it and is little documented for this plant specifically.
harvest_season: Little is documented for this plant. As with other Hunan teas, spring pickings are normally the most valued.
appearance_dry: Little is documented; depends on the tea made from the leaf.
appearance_liquor: Little is documented; depends on the tea made, a light yellow-green if made as a green tea.
appearance_wet: Little is documented; the name points to a large leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting record exists for this plant on its own; the cup depends on how the leaf is processed.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a green tea only; follow the style of the tea actually bought.

vintage_note: Not normally sold as a labelled product in its own right. Teas from the area are sold according to class, so green tea would be the current spring harvest; ask the seller what was made from the leaf and when.
description:
Yuntai Shan Zhong, also called Yuntai Shan large-leaf, is a tea plant linked with the Yuntai Shan area of Anhua County in Hunan, a place better known to most drinkers for its dark tea.

Very little is documented about it in detail. The name tells you the place and suggests a large leaf; tree form, chemistry and exact processing are not well recorded in anything easy to find.

The mountain itself is a working tea landscape, with gardens on its slopes and at its summit. Local lists of Hunan teas mention this plant alongside other regional types.

Take any bag named after it as a question to ask rather than a promise: who made it, what kind of tea, and from which harvest.
history: Little is documented about its origin or whether and when it was formally registered. What can be said is that it is known by name in the Anhua area of Hunan and is listed among the province's local tea types.
